edges.description: The mouse null does not model the human disease because it does not survive to have one. Human patients homozygous for truncating MTRFR alleles are born, develop normally for months to years, and present in childhood; the equivalent mouse dies in utero. That is a qualitative species difference in tolerance of the same genotype, not a difference in severity, and it is recorded as a failure rather than as partial recapitulation because there is no phenotype in the homozygote to compare with a patient's.
edges.limitations:
The lethality is not marginal and it is not an artefact of a badly chosen allele. Homozygous embryos are recovered at the expected frequency at E10.5 and E11.5 and none at all from E12.5 onward, using an allele that should retain partial activity by extrapolation from the human truncation series - so a genotype milder than several human ones is still lethal in mid-gestation. The authors' conclusion is that mice are more sensitive to loss of Mtrfr than humans are.
Embryonic lethality means no untreated homozygous animal exists to characterise, so every observation in this line comes from transgene-rescued animals. The rescue therefore tests whether supplying MTRFR prevents the mouse phenotype, which is a different question from whether supplying it helps a patient whose disease has already begun. The transgene is human MTRFR expressed from a non-native promoter, so neither its level nor its tissue distribution matches endogenous expression.
edges.source: Mtrfr K155* knock-in mouse with human MTRFR transgene rescue

edges.description: What the line does establish. One copy of a wild-type MTRFR transgene completely rescues the homozygous truncating genotype, and a partially functional transgene rescues less well - a dose-and-function relationship that is the argument for gene replacement being a coherent strategy for this gene.
edges.limitations: Rescue was prevention, delivered from conception by a transgene rather than to an affected animal. Nothing here shows that restoring MTRFR reverses established optic atrophy, neuropathy or spasticity, and the human diagnostic delay is a median of 17 years. The absence of overexpression toxicity in vivo is reassuring but was measured in animals whose alternative was death in utero.
edges.source: Mtrfr K155* knock-in mouse with human MTRFR transgene rescue

edges.description: The fish tolerates the genotype the mouse cannot and the human tolerates imperfectly, so it sits at the permissive extreme of a three-species range. What it contributes is a demonstration that losing mitoribosome rescue is survivable in a vertebrate and that the cost appears under stress - which is a candidate explanation for why the human disease is progressive and tissue-selective rather than lethal.
edges.limitations: Healthy and fertile knockouts do not develop optic atrophy, neuropathy or spasticity, so none of the disease's defining features is modelled. The authors invoke compensatory mechanisms specific to teleosts, including the observation that teleost Ict1 lacks the large-subunit binding motif found in most metazoans so that Mtrfr may partially compensate for Ict1 loss - a compensation structure that does not exist in humans. Whatever makes the fish healthy is therefore probably not what makes the human patient survive.

nodes.description: A length-dependent axonal motor-predominant neuropathy, reported in 80 percent of the 27-patient review, which places it in the 80 to 99 percent band. It is prominent enough that the disease reaches some patients through a neuromuscular clinic as a CMT6-like axonal neuropathy with optic atrophy. Distal weakness, foot drop and muscle wasting in the hands are the usual findings; electrophysiology shows a widespread lower motor neuron lesion.

nodes.description: The four complexes built partly from mitochondrially encoded subunits fail together, and complex II - encoded entirely in the nucleus - is spared. The pattern reported in the founding patients is a severe decrease in complexes I, IV and V with a smaller decrease in complex III. Individual patients depart from that: one had isolated complex IV deficiency at 40 percent of control values with complexes I, II and III normal, another had complex V assembly and activity reduced with a fall in respiration rate and mitochondrial membrane potential. A normal assay on one complex in one tissue therefore does not exclude the diagnosis.

nodes.description:
The clinical selectivity of COXPD7 is the selectivity of a bioenergetic disease. Retinal ganglion cells with long unmyelinated intraretinal axons, corticospinal tract neurons and long peripheral motor axons are the cells that fail, which is why the disease presents as optic atrophy plus spastic paraparesis plus axonal neuropathy rather than as a generalised encephalopathy. Nerve biopsy in one family showed loss of large myelinated and unmyelinated fibres, and electrophysiology in the Behr-phenotype series localised widespread lower motor neuron and anterior horn cell lesions.
The cell-selectivity argument is inference. It is the standard reasoning applied to mitochondrial optic neuropathies and it fits the phenotype, but no study has measured respiratory chain function in a patient's retinal ganglion cells or corticospinal neurons, and the fibroblasts and lymphoblasts that were assayed are not the cells that die.

nodes.description:
Without MTRFR, a mitoribosome that stalls during elongation is not cleared. The nascent chain stays attached, the ribosome is not recycled, and the pool of ribosomes available for productive synthesis shrinks. This node is where the disease's specificity lies: MTRFR does not read stop codons, so the lesion is not a failure to finish normal proteins but a failure to recover from abnormal termination events.
A sibling factor, ICT1, performs a related rescue and is additionally a structural protein of the mitochondrial large ribosomal subunit, which is why its loss is lethal where MTRFR loss is not. That difference is the reason a human can live with no MTRFR at all.

nodes.description: Synthesis of all thirteen mitochondrially encoded polypeptides falls together, uniformly rather than selectively. Patient fibroblasts show that decrease directly, and the controls that make it interpretable are all negative: steady-state levels of mitochondrial mRNAs, tRNAs and rRNAs are not reduced, and neither are the mitochondrial translation elongation factors or the protein components of the mitoribosome. Nothing is missing from the apparatus; the apparatus is not turning over.

nodes.description:
Raised serum lactate, the expected biochemical readout of a combined oxidative phosphorylation defect, and a lactate peak on brainstem magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Neither is constant: the spectroscopy peak was seen in only 3 of 11 patients in one pooled series, and the severe Leigh-presenting patient in whom serum lactate was followed had values from 19 to 69 mg/dL against a 4.5 to 14.4 mg/dL reference interval during a terminal deterioration rather than at baseline.
No frequency band is recorded. The MRS peak was reported in 3 of 11, which would be OCCASIONAL, but serum lactate was not systematically measured across the reviewed patients and the two measurements are not the same quantity; banding on the imaging figure would misstate how often the blood test is abnormal.

nodes.description:
Biallelic truncating MTRFR alleles. The reported spectrum is uniformly null: nonsense, frameshift and splice-site changes, including one synonymous variant that acts as a frameshift by abolishing a splice site and retaining an intron. Eleven distinct pathogenic variants were catalogued across the first 27 reported patients.
Position within the protein carries the severity. The GGQ-containing domain is encoded by the first coding exon, and truncations that disrupt it are expected to be more severe; C-terminal truncations, which leave more of the protein intact, tend to spare cognition.

nodes.description: A gene-replacement feasibility study built on a mouse that should not exist. A truncating K155* allele was engineered; homozygotes die embryonically while heterozygotes are normal. Transgenic strains expressing wild-type or partially functional human MTRFR were then crossed in: a single copy of the wild-type transgene completely rescued the homozygous phenotype, the mutant transgene rescued less efficiently, and detailed evaluation of the rescued animals found no abnormalities. Neither transgene caused adverse effects in vivo, despite dose-dependent phenotypes from overexpression in cell culture.

nodes.description:
The near-constant feature and, in almost every reported patient, the first one. Onset is in childhood - age 5 to 6 years in the Behr-phenotype siblings - and cranial MRI showed optic nerve atrophy in all eleven patients of one pooled series. In one series the optic atrophy remained stable while the other neurological signs progressed, so it is the presenting sign rather than the one that drives deterioration.
Banded VERY_FREQUENT on the reported 92.3 percent, which falls in the 80 to 99 percent band. That figure is a proportion of published cases and is subject to ascertainment bias - a patient without optic atrophy is less likely to have been tested for this gene - so it should not be read as a population penetrance.
